nodes.name: Wild figs
nodes.desc: Fig trees fruit through much of the year and feed many forest animals. Gibbons and hornbills both rely heavily on figs.

nodes.name: Jambolan (Java plum)
nodes.desc: A fruiting forest tree. GloBI records elephants, macaques, squirrels and many birds eating its fruit.

nodes.name: Malabar melastome
nodes.desc: A shrub of open and disturbed ground. GloBI records elephants and macaques eating it.

nodes.name: Cogon grass
nodes.desc: A tall grass of the open grasslands on the plateau, grazed by large herbivores such as elephants and sambar.

nodes.name: White-handed gibbon
nodes.desc: Mostly eats fruit (about half its diet), plus leaves, insects and flowers; figs are a favourite. Long-term studies of its social life were done at Khao Yai.

nodes.name: Great hornbill
nodes.desc: Eats mostly fruit, especially figs, and gets its water from fruit. Also catches small animals. A seed disperser for many forest trees.

nodes.name: Northern pig-tailed macaque
nodes.desc: One of the most recorded mammals around the park. GloBI records it eating fruit and shrubs such as jambolan and melastome.

nodes.name: Finlayson's squirrel
nodes.desc: A common tree squirrel. GloBI records it eating jambolan fruit and other fruit.

nodes.name: Forest insects
nodes.desc: Moths, beetles, ants and other insects feed on leaves, nectar and fruit and are food for bats, toads, gibbons and birds.

nodes.name: Indian muntjac
nodes.desc: A small forest deer that browses and eats fallen fruit. Prey of dholes and tigers.

nodes.name: Sambar
nodes.desc: A large deer that eats grasses, leaves and fruit. A favourite prey of tigers; dholes and leopards take young or sick animals.

nodes.name: Asian elephant
nodes.desc: A generalist grazer and browser eating grasses, bark and many other plants. Tigers have been recorded killing calves.

nodes.name: Wrinkle-lipped bat
nodes.desc: Lives in large cave colonies and flies out to feed on night-flying insects. Its droppings enrich cave and soil nutrients.

nodes.name: Asian common toad
nodes.desc: A common amphibian that eats insects. GloBI records water monitors eating it.

nodes.name: Common water monitor
nodes.desc: A big lizard that eats amphibians and other small animals, and also scavenges.

nodes.name: Golden jackal
nodes.desc: An opportunist hunter and scavenger. GloBI records it eating sambar.

nodes.name: Tiger
nodes.desc: Top predator. Camera traps recorded 18 tigers in the park in 2016-17. Sambar are a favourite prey and calves of elephants can be killed.

nodes.name: Dhole
nodes.desc: A pack-hunting wild dog that takes medium and large deer such as sambar and muntjac, mostly avoiding the tiger's largest prey.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: The wet season rains soak the evergreen forest and drive the fruiting of figs and other trees.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives growth in the forest canopy and the open grasslands.

nodes.name: Soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients in the forest soil, topped up by decay and bat droppings, feed the plants.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead leaves, fallen fruit, droppings and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
